config.description: Method replication: the images are new Baidu street views of the seven central districts of Wuhan (one of four directions at each point), not the paper's labelled images. Each street view is judged as unsafe, neutral or safe from the overall impression of walking there, one image at a time with no place names, as the ten annotators did in Chen & Tang (2025, Sustainability). The paper used these three-level labels to train a model that mapped safety across 43,232 street points. Annotators were told not to overreact to big roads, and that busy centres, quiet suburbs or more or less greenery are not by themselves safe or unsafe; this guidance is shown in the introduction. Differences from the original study: (1) 40 random views per participant; (2) the paper's annotators had GIS expertise or at least one year living in Wuhan, recorded here with two questions.

paper.title: Assessing Urban Safety Perception Through Street View Imagery and Transfer Learning: A Case Study of Wuhan, China
